rationale:
Decision: split into six children. Five reuse comparator-accepted declarations at their byte-identical frozen types: the controller links the existing accepted nodes and no new proof work is created. One child is new: mass_bound, Submission.dor_lmb_ic_measure_le_of_weighted_orient_eq.

Why not a leaf. A childless node's candidate may append exactly one helper-free theorem. It would sit on this node's proof base 427b834, which contains none of the cross-branch declarations. The whole supplied proof would then have to be re-proved inside a single theorem, about 1,300 lines in the accepted code:
- tangent locality and the orientation sign;
- the construction and every IMRep field;
- integration of (†), the orientation normalisation and the mass bound.
That duplicates accepted subtrees. With the split, the only new work is a roughly 90-line leaf plus a 4-line parent assembly.

How the supplied proof maps to the children:
- Step 1(a) → orientation_pairing (regcomp_unit_orientation_pairing): Simon 6.2.6(a)–(b) for the Euclidean coefficient norm.
- Step 1(b) → orientation_sign (rsdic_unitOrientation_eq_or_eq_neg).
- Locality, used in steps 3(b), 6(e) and 6(f) → tangent_locality (rsdic_ae_tangent_iff_of_subset). Its type is byte-identical to the sibling dor_lmb_approx_tangent_locality. That sibling cannot be a dependency of this node's children, so the accepted declaration is reused instead.
- Steps 2–6 and (†) → combination_construction (rsdic_exists_imrep_int_combination), which depends on tangent_locality and orientation_sign.
- Step 7 → combination_action (rsdic_imrep_action_int_combination).
- The multiplicity bound at the end of step 5, together with step 8 → mass_bound (new), which depends on orientation_pairing.

Parent assembly (checked in Lean):
1. combination_construction P n U R₁ R₂ p₁ p₂ hU gives R with the identity (†) a.e.
2. For every ω, the hypotheses and combination_action give S ω = p₁T₁ ω + p₂T₂ ω = p₁R₁.action ω + p₂R₂.action ω = R.action ω, so R.Represents S.
3. mass_bound gives R.measure ≤ (p₁.natAbs : ℝ≥0∞) • R₁.measure + (p₂.natAbs : ℝ≥0∞) • R₂.measure.
The Lean proof is: obtain ⟨R, hR⟩ := …construction…; refine ⟨R, fun ω => ?_, …mass_bound… hR⟩; rw [hS ω, h₁ ω, h₂ ω, …action… hR ω].

Two departures, both stated in the child proofs:

subproblems.title: Locality of approximate tangent spaces (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2)); reused Submission.rsdic_ae_tangent_iff_of_subset
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, and let A ⊆ B ⊆ U be Borel sets with Hⁿ(B ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then for Hⁿ⌞A-almost every x, simultaneously for every linear subspace Q of ℝ^P: B has approximate tangent space Q at x (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q, Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4) if and only if A has approximate tangent space Q at x.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U A B : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet A → MeasurableSet B → A ⊆ B → B ⊆ U → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (B ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict A), ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2) and the proof of Theorem 1.6 "⇒" (chapter-03.txt lines 86–90 and 113–143), which compares blow-ups by the Upper Density Theorem, Ch. 1, 3.6 and Remark 3.7 (chapter-01.txt lines 700–712). In the supplied proof of the selected theorem this locality fact is invoked in steps 3(b), 6(e) and 6(f) as "tangent_locality". The selected node's sibling of that name cannot be a dependency of its children, so the fact is supplied here as the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.rsdic_ae_tangent_iff_of_subset, reused at its frozen type; that type is byte-identical to the sibling's. The argument below expands the one the parent decomposition supplied for that sibling. The accepted Lean proof of this declaration takes a different route (a Besicovitch density ratio plus a growth bound); either argument proves this exact statement.
Notation: μ := μHE[n], which equals SimonGMT's Hausdorff measure of natural dimension n (simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure) and is Borel regular. B̄_ρ(z) is the closed ball. η_{x,λ}(z) := λ⁻¹(z − x) is SimonGMT's blowUpMap x λ. All integrals over sets are Bochner integrals for the restricted measure.
1. Exhaustion. If U = ∅ then A = ∅ and there is nothing to prove. Otherwise choose open sets V_m (m ≥ 1) with U = ⋃_m V_m, each with compact closure K_m ⊆ U:
 - if U = ℝ^P, take V_m := {|x| < m};
 - otherwise take V_m := {x : |x| < m, dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ U) > 1/m}. Then K_m ⊆ {|x| ≤ m, dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ U) ≥ 1/m}, a compact subset of U. Every x ∈ U lies in some V_m, because ℝ^P ∖ U is closed and does not contain x.
2. Upper density. Put D := B ∖ A, a Borel set. For each m, D_m := D ∩ V_m is Borel and μ(D_m) ≤ μ(B ∩ K_m) < ∞ by hypothesis. Apply the Upper Density Theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 3.6, with Simon's μ := Hⁿ; formalized as SimonGMT simon_theorem_3_6 / simon_remark_3_7_hausdorff in Chapter01/DensityComparison.lean, cited here as a book theorem) to the μ-measurable set D_m of finite measure. It gives limsup_{ρ↓0} μ(D_m ∩ B̄_ρ(x))/ρⁿ = 0 for μ-a.e. x ∉ D_m. Let E_m be the exceptional μ-null set and E := ⋃_m E_m, again μ-null.
3. Vanishing density of D. Let x ∈ A ∖ E. Then x ∉ D (as A ∩ D = ∅), and x ∈ V_m for some m (as A ⊆ U). Choose ρ₀ > 0 with B̄_{ρ₀}(x) ⊆ V_m. For 0 < ρ ≤ ρ₀ we have D ∩ B̄_ρ(x) = D_m ∩ B̄_ρ(x). Since x ∉ D_m and x ∉ E_m,
 (∗) ρ^{−n} μ(D ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) → 0 as ρ ↓ 0.
4. Comparison of blow-ups. Fix such an x and f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ). Choose R ≥ 1 with f = 0 outside B̄_R(0), and put S := sup|f| < ∞. Let 0 < λ < ρ₀/R and η := η_{x,λ}.
 (a) η is an affine bijection and a homeomorphism of ℝ^P. Hence η(A), η(B), η(D) are Borel, and η(B) is the disjoint union of η(A) and η(D).
 (b) μ is translation invariant and μ(cZ) = |c|ⁿ μ(Z) (Mathlib Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀). Since η(Z) ∩ B̄_R(0) = η(Z ∩ B̄_{λR}(x)), this gives μ(η(Z) ∩ B̄_R(0)) = λ^{−n} μ(Z ∩ B̄_{λR}(x)) for every set Z. In particular μ(η(B) ∩ B̄_R(0)) ≤ λ^{−n} μ(B ∩ K_m) < ∞, because B̄_{λR}(x) ⊆ B̄_{ρ₀}(x) ⊆ K_m.
 (c) f is bounded and vanishes outside B̄_R(0), so it is integrable on η(B) and on its Borel subsets η(A), η(D). By additivity over the disjoint pieces, ∫_{η(B)} f dμ − ∫_{η(A)} f dμ = ∫_{η(D)} f dμ.
 (d) By (b), |∫_{η(D)} f dμ| ≤ S·μ(η(D) ∩ B̄_R(0)) = S·λ^{−n} μ(D ∩ B̄_{λR}(x)) = S·Rⁿ·(λR)^{−n} μ(D ∩ B̄_{λR}(x)). This tends to 0 as λ ↓ 0 by (∗), since λR ↓ 0. For n = 0 the same computation holds with λ^{−n} = Rⁿ = 1.
 Hence ∫_{η_{x,λ}(B)} f dμ − ∫_{η_{x,λ}(A)} f dμ → 0 as λ ↓ 0, for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ).
5. Conclusion. Let x ∈ A ∖ E and let Q be a linear subspace of ℝ^P. HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q both consist of:
 - the condition dim Q = n, common to both;
 - the convergence, for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), of the blow-up integrals ∫_{η_{x,λ}(·)} f dμ to ∫_Q f dμ as λ ↓ 0.
 By step 4 the blow-up integrals of B and of A differ by a quantity tending to 0, so those of B converge to ∫_Q f dμ if and only if those of A do. Thus B has approximate tangent space Q at x if and only if A does. The null set E does not depend on Q, and μ⌞A(E) = 0. Hence the equivalence holds for μ⌞A-a.e. x, simultaneously for every Q. ∎
proof_key_steps: Exhaust U by countably many open V_m with compact closures K_m ⊆ U; D := B ∖ A has μ(D ∩ V_m) < ∞.
Upper Density Theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 3.6): ρ^{−n}μ(D ∩ V_m ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) → 0 for μ-a.e. x ∉ D ∩ V_m; collect a single null set E.
For x ∈ A ∖ E, localize to get ρ^{−n}μ(D ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) → 0.
So the defining limits of Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 for A and for B coincide; the equivalence holds off E for all Q.

subproblems.title: Two unit orientations of one subspace differ by a sign; reused Submission.rsdic_unitOrientation_eq_or_eq_neg
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let Q be a linear subspace of ℝ^P and let v, w ∈ Λₙ(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P n). If v and w are both unit orientations of Q (IsUnitOrientationOf v Q and IsUnitOrientationOf w Q: v(α) = ±α(τ), w(α) = ±α(τ′) for orthonormal families τ, τ′ spanning Q and all n-covectors α), then w = v or w = −v.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (v w : MultiVector P n) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), IsUnitOrientationOf v Q → IsUnitOrientationOf w Q → w = v ∨ w = -v
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1(b) of the supplied proof of the selected theorem: orthonormal bases of Q differ by an orthogonal matrix, so α(τ') = det(O)α(τ) and ζ' = ±ζ. This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.rsdic_unitOrientation_eq_or_eq_neg, reused at its byte-identical frozen type.
1. Unfolding the hypotheses. There are orthonormal families τ, τ' : Fin n → ℝ^P with span(range τ) = Q = span(range τ'). There are also signs ε, ε' ∈ {1, −1} with v(α) = ε·α(τ) and w(α) = ε'·α(τ') for every n-covector α (a continuous alternating n-linear map ℝ^P → ℝ).
2. Orthonormal bases. Each τ_i and τ'_i lies in Q, and both families stay orthonormal in the inner product space Q. τ is linearly independent and spans Q, so dim Q = n. An orthonormal, hence linearly independent, family of n vectors in the n-dimensional space Q spans Q. Hence τ and τ' are orthonormal bases b and b' of Q, indexed by Fin n.
3. Determinant. Let d := det_b(b'), the determinant of the change-of-basis matrix from b to b'. Both bases are orthonormal, so this matrix is orthogonal and d ∈ {1, −1} (Mathlib OrthonormalBasis.det_to_matrix_orthonormalBasis_real).
4. Restriction. Let α be an n-covector and α_Q its restriction to Q (α composed with the inclusion Q → ℝ^P in each slot). α_Q is an alternating n-linear form on the n-dimensional space Q, so α_Q = α_Q(b)·det_b (Mathlib AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det). Evaluating at b' gives α(τ') = α_Q(b') = α_Q(b)·det_b(b') = d·α(τ). The number d does not depend on α.
5. Conclusion. For every α, w(α) = ε'·α(τ') = ε'd·α(τ) = (εε'd)·(ε·α(τ)) = s·v(α), where s := εε'd ∈ {1, −1} (using ε² = 1). Hence w = s·v: w = v if s = 1 and w = −v if s = −1. For n = 0 the same argument applies: τ = τ' is the empty family, Q = {0} and d = 1. ∎
proof_key_steps: Both orthonormal families spanning Q are orthonormal bases b, b' of Q.
det_b(b') = ±1 because the change-of-basis matrix between orthonormal bases is orthogonal.
Every n-covector restricted to Q is a multiple of det_b, so α(τ') = det_b(b')·α(τ) for all α.
Hence w = (εε'det_b(b'))·v with εε'det_b(b') ∈ {±1}.

subproblems.title: An IMRep R with 1_Mθξ = p₁1_{M₁}θ₁ξ₁ + p₂1_{M₂}θ₂ξ₂ a.e.; reused Submission.rsdic_exists_imrep_int_combination
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, let R₁ = (M₁, θ₁, ξ₁) and R₂ = (M₂, θ₂, ξ₂) be integer multiplicity triples (IMRep) in U, and let p₁, p₂ ∈ ℤ. Then there is an IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) in U such that for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ ℝ^P (Hⁿ = μHE[n]) the n-vectors satisfy 1_M(x)θ(x)ξ(x) = p₁1_{M₁}(x)θ₁(x)ξ₁(x) + p₂1_{M₂}(x)θ₂(x)ξ₂(x) (Set.indicator and real scalar multiplication in MultiVector P n).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R₁ R₂ : IMRep U n) (p₁ p₂ : ℤ), IsOpen U → ∃ R : IMRep U n, ∀ᵐ x ∂μHE[n], R.carrier.indicator (fun y => (R.mult y : ℝ) • R.orient y) x = (p₁ : ℝ) • R₁.carrier.indicator (fun y => (R₁.mult y : ℝ) • R₁.orient y) x + (p₂ : ℝ) • R₂.carrier.indicator (fun y => (R₂.mult y : ℝ) • R₂.orient y) x
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2–6 of the supplied proof of the selected theorem, which give the identity (†) of its step 5. This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.rsdic_exists_imrep_int_combination, reused at its byte-identical frozen type. Simon states the underlying fact without proof (Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(1), chapter-06.txt lines 755–756).
One deliberate departure: the Borel sign σ of step 3(c) is replaced by an equality test (step 4 below). The supplied coordinate test Σ_I ξ̃₁(dx^I)ξ̃₂(dx^I) ≥ 0 needs Cauchy–Binet for its verification, and only the property ξ̃₂ = σξ̃₁ a.e. on M₁ ∩ M₂ is used later.
Notation:
 - μ := μHE[n]; Mᵢ := Rᵢ.carrier, θᵢ := Rᵢ.mult, ξᵢ := Rᵢ.orient (i = 1, 2); M' := M₁ ∪ M₂.
 - For c ∈ ℤ, |c| ∈ ℕ is its absolute value and sgn(c) ∈ {−1, 0, 1} its sign.
 - "For μ-a.e. x ∈ S" (S Borel) means μ⌞S-a.e., i.e. for μ-a.e. x, x ∈ S ⇒ ….
 - HasATS stands for HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n.
1. Local finiteness (step 2(a)). Let K ⊆ U be compact. θᵢ is ℕ-valued and positive on Mᵢ (mult_pos), so θᵢ ≥ 1 on Mᵢ. Hence μ(Mᵢ ∩ K) ≤ ∫⁻_{Mᵢ∩K} θᵢ dμ < ∞ (locallyIntegrable_mult). Consequently every Borel C ⊆ M' satisfies μ(C ∩ K) ≤ μ(M₁ ∩ K) + μ(M₂ ∩ K) < ∞. Also M' is Borel and M' ⊆ U.
2. Tangent transfer (steps 3(a)–(b) and 6(e), from the sibling tangent_locality). Claim (T): let i ∈ {1, 2} and let B, C be Borel sets with B ⊆ Mᵢ and B ⊆ C ⊆ M'. Then for μ-a.e. x ∈ B there is a linear subspace Q with HasATS C x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξᵢ x) Q.
 Proof of (T):
 (a) The field orients of Rᵢ holds μ-a.e. on Mᵢ, hence μ-a.e. on B ⊆ Mᵢ. It gives Q with HasATS Mᵢ x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξᵢ x) Q.
 (b) Apply tangent_locality to the pair (B, Mᵢ): B ⊆ Mᵢ ⊆ U are Borel and μ(Mᵢ ∩ K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U by step 1. So for μ-a.e. x ∈ B and every Q, HasATS Mᵢ x Q ↔ HasATS B x Q.
 (c) Apply tangent_locality to the pair (B, C): B ⊆ C ⊆ U are Borel and μ(C ∩ K) < ∞ by step 1. So for μ-a.e. x ∈ B and every Q, HasATS C x Q ↔ HasATS B x Q.
 (d) At the μ-a.e. points of B where (a)–(c) all hold, the plane Q from (a) satisfies HasATS Mᵢ x Q ⇒ HasATS B x Q ⇒ HasATS C x Q. ∎(T)
3. Borel versions (step 2(b)). ξᵢ is AEStronglyMeasurable for μ⌞Mᵢ. Choose a strongly measurable (Borel) ξ̃ᵢ : ℝ^P → Λₙ(ℝ^P) with ξ̃ᵢ = ξᵢ μ-a.e. on Mᵢ (Mathlib AEStronglyMeasurable.mk, ae_eq_mk).
4. Overlap sign (step 3).
 (a) Apply (T) with i = 1 and with i = 2, both times with B = C = M₁ ∩ M₂. For μ-a.e. x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂ this gives planes Q₁, Q₂ with HasATS (M₁ ∩ M₂) x Qᵢ and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξᵢ x) Qᵢ.
 (b) Approximate tangent spaces are unique (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(1); SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique), so Q₁ = Q₂. The sibling orientation_sign then gives ξ₂(x) = ξ₁(x) or ξ₂(x) = −ξ₁(x). With step 3, ξ̃₂(x) = ±ξ̃₁(x) for μ-a.e. x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂.
 (c) Define σ(x) := 1 if ξ̃₂(x) = ξ̃₁(x), and σ(x) := −1 otherwise. The set {ξ̃₂ = ξ̃₁} is Borel (both maps are strongly measurable into the metrizable space Λₙ(ℝ^P)), so σ is Borel.
 (d) For μ-a.e. x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂, ξ̃₂(x) = σ(x)ξ̃₁(x): if ξ̃₂(x) = ξ̃₁(x) then σ(x) = 1; otherwise ξ̃₂(x) = −ξ̃₁(x) and σ(x) = −1.
5. Definition of R (step 4).
 (a) Let c(x) := p₁θ₁(x)1_{M₁}(x) + p₂θ₂(x)(σ(x)1_{M₁∩M₂}(x) + 1_{M₂∖M₁}(x)). This is the supplied m: p₁θ₁ + σp₂θ₂ on M₁ ∩ M₂, p₁θ₁ on M₁ ∖ M₂, p₂θ₂ on M₂ ∖ M₁ and 0 off M'.
 (b) Let ζ(x) := ξ̃₁(x) for x ∈ M₁ and ζ(x) := ξ̃₂(x) otherwise.
 (c) c : ℝ^P → ℤ is Borel (built from Borel maps and indicators of Borel sets; ℤ is discrete), and ζ is strongly measurable.
 (d) Let M := {x ∈ M' : c(x) ≠ 0}, θ := |c| (ℕ-valued) and ξ := sgn(c)·ζ. On M this is the supplied ξ: sgn(m)ξ̃₁ on M₁ and sgn(m)ξ̃₂ on M₂ ∖ M₁.
 Two properties follow:
 (5a) 1_M(x)θ(x)ξ(x) = c(x)ζ(x) for every x. Indeed |c|·sgn(c) = c, and c(x) = 0 whenever x ∉ M.
 (5b) |c(x)| ≤ |p₁|θ₁(x)1_{M₁}(x) + |p₂|θ₂(x)1_{M₂}(x) for every x. This is the triangle inequality: |σ| = 1, and 1_{M₁∩M₂} + 1_{M₂∖M₁} = 1_{M₂} with at most one term nonzero.
6. R is an IMRep in U (step 6).
 (a) M is Borel and M ⊆ M' ⊆ U.
 (b) M' is countably n-rectifiable by SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_iUnion, applied to the sequence M₁, M₂, M₂, … (fields rectifiable). Hence so is M ⊆ M' (CountablyRectifiable.mono).
 (c) θ = |c| is Borel, and θ ≥ 1 > 0 on M.
 (d) For compact K ⊆ U, (5b) gives ∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dμ ≤ |p₁|∫⁻_{M₁∩K} θ₁ dμ + |p₂|∫⁻_{M₂∩K} θ₂ dμ < ∞.
 (e) ξ is strongly measurable, hence AEStronglyMeasurable for μ⌞M.
 (f) Orientation on M ∩ M₁. Apply (T) with i = 1, B := M ∩ M₁, C := M. For μ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ M₁ there is Q with HasATS M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ₁ x) Q, and ξ₁(x) = ξ̃₁(x) = ζ(x) by step 3. Since c(x) ≠ 0, ξ(x) = ±ξ₁(x). A unit orientation multiplied by −1 is a unit orientation of the same plane (same τ, the other sign alternative). So IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q.
 (g) Orientation on M ∖ M₁. Apply (T) with i = 2, B := M ∖ M₁ (⊆ M₂ because M ⊆ M₁ ∪ M₂) and C := M. Here ξ₂(x) = ξ̃₂(x) = ζ(x) and ξ(x) = ±ξ₂(x), so the same conclusion holds.
 Since M = (M ∩ M₁) ∪ (M ∖ M₁), (f) and (g) give the field orients μ⌞M-a.e. Thus R := (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U.
7. The identity (†) (step 5). By steps 3 and 4, for μ-a.e. x:
 (i) x ∈ Mᵢ ⇒ ξ̃ᵢ(x) = ξᵢ(x), for i = 1, 2;
 (ii) x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂ ⇒ ξ̃₂(x) = σ(x)ξ̃₁(x).
 Fix such an x. By (i), p₁1_{M₁}θ₁ξ₁ + p₂1_{M₂}θ₂ξ₂ = p₁1_{M₁}θ₁ξ̃₁ + p₂1_{M₂}θ₂ξ̃₂ at x, since each indicator vanishes off its set. This equals c(x)ζ(x), by cases:
 - x ∉ M': both sides are 0;
 - x ∈ M₁ ∖ M₂: both equal p₁θ₁(x)ξ̃₁(x);
 - x ∈ M₂ ∖ M₁: both equal p₂θ₂(x)ξ̃₂(x);
 - x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂: by (ii) the left side is (p₁θ₁(x) + p₂θ₂(x)σ(x))ξ̃₁(x) = c(x)ζ(x).
 By (5a), c(x)ζ(x) = 1_M(x)θ(x)ξ(x). Hence 1_Mθξ = p₁1_{M₁}θ₁ξ₁ + p₂1_{M₂}θ₂ξ₂ μ-a.e., which is the assertion. ∎
proof_key_steps: Local finiteness of M₁ ∪ M₂ (θᵢ ≥ 1); Borel versions ξ̃ᵢ of the orientations.
Tangent transfer (T) from tangent_locality: for a.e. x ∈ B ⊆ Mᵢ, ξᵢ(x) orients an approximate tangent plane of any Borel C with B ⊆ C ⊆ M₁ ∪ M₂.
On M₁ ∩ M₂ the tangent planes coincide, so ξ₂ = ±ξ₁ by orientation_sign; the Borel sign σ := 1 on {ξ̃₂ = ξ̃₁}, −1 elsewhere, gives ξ̃₂ = σξ̃₁ a.e. there.
c := p₁θ₁1_{M₁} + p₂θ₂(σ1_{M₁∩M₂} + 1_{M₂∖M₁}), M := {c ≠ 0} ∩ (M₁ ∪ M₂), θ := |c|, ξ := sgn(c)ζ; then 1_Mθξ = cζ and |c| ≤ |p₁|θ₁1_{M₁} + |p₂|θ₂1_{M₂}.
Verify every IMRep field (orientation via (T) on M ∩ M₁ and M ∖ M₁) and the identity 1_Mθξ = p₁1_{M₁}θ₁ξ₁ + p₂1_{M₂}θ₂ξ₂ a.e. by cases.

subproblems.title: Integrating the a.e. identity: R.action = p₁R₁.action + p₂R₂.action; reused Submission.rsdic_imrep_action_int_combination
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, let R₁ = (M₁, θ₁, ξ₁), R₂ = (M₂, θ₂, ξ₂), R = (M, θ, ξ) be IMReps in U and p₁, p₂ ∈ ℤ. Suppose that for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ ℝ^P (Hⁿ = μHE[n]) 1_M(x)θ(x)ξ(x) = p₁1_{M₁}(x)θ₁(x)ξ₁(x) + p₂1_{M₂}(x)θ₂(x)ξ₂(x) in Λₙ(ℝ^P). Then for every test form ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), R.action ω = p₁·R₁.action ω + p₂·R₂.action ω, where R′.action ω = ∫_{M′} θ′(x)⟨ω(x), ξ′(x)⟩ dHⁿ(x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R₁ R₂ R : IMRep U n) (p₁ p₂ : ℤ), (∀ᵐ x ∂μHE[n], R.carrier.indicator (fun y => (R.mult y : ℝ) • R.orient y) x = (p₁ : ℝ) • R₁.carrier.indicator (fun y => (R₁.mult y : ℝ) • R₁.orient y) x + (p₂ : ℝ) • R₂.carrier.indicator (fun y => (R₂.mult y : ℝ) • R₂.orient y) x) → ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, R.action (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) = (p₁ : ℝ) * R₁.action (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) + (p₂ : ℝ) * R₂.action (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 7 of the supplied proof of the selected theorem (integration of the pointwise identity (†), with the bound of step 1(a)). This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.rsdic_imrep_action_int_combination, reused at its byte-identical frozen type.
Notation:
 - μ := μHE[n].
 - For an IMRep R' = (M', θ', ξ') in U put F_{R'}(x) := 1_{M'}(x)θ'(x)ξ'(x) ∈ Λₙ(ℝ^P). The hypothesis reads F_R = p₁F_{R₁} + p₂F_{R₂} μ-a.e.
 - Fix a test form ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). It is smooth, hence continuous, and has compact support K := tsupport ω ⊆ U; ω(x) = 0 for x ∉ K. Put W := sup_x ‖ω(x)‖ < ∞ (operator norm on n-covectors).
1. Norm bound (step 1(a)). Let v be a unit orientation of some Q, i.e. v(α) = ±α(τ) for an orthonormal τ. Then |v(α)| = |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏ᵢ‖τᵢ‖ = ‖α‖ for every n-covector α (Mathlib ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm).
2. Integrability. Let R' = (M', θ', ξ') be any IMRep in U and h(x) := θ'(x)ξ'(x)(ω(x)).
 - h is AEStronglyMeasurable for μ⌞M': θ' is Borel, ξ' is AEStronglyMeasurable for μ⌞M', ω is continuous, and evaluation (L, α) ↦ L(α) is continuous.
 - By the field orients and step 1, for μ⌞M'-a.e. x we have |h(x)| ≤ θ'(x)‖ω(x)‖ ≤ W·θ'(x)1_K(x).
 - The bound is integrable on M': its integral is W·∫⁻_{M'∩K} θ' dμ < ∞ by locallyIntegrable_mult (K is compact and K ⊆ U).
 Hence h is integrable on M'.
3. Rewriting the action. For R' as in step 2 and every x, F_{R'}(x)(ω(x)) = 1_{M'}(x)h(x). M' is Borel, so R'.action ω = ∫_{M'} h dμ = ∫_{ℝ^P} F_{R'}(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x), and x ↦ F_{R'}(x)(ω(x)) is μ-integrable by step 2.
4. Conclusion. Evaluate the hypothesis at ω(x): F_R(x)(ω(x)) = p₁F_{R₁}(x)(ω(x)) + p₂F_{R₂}(x)(ω(x)) for μ-a.e. x. Integrate over ℝ^P. Integrals of a.e.-equal functions agree, and the Bochner integral is linear on the integrable functions of step 3. Using step 3 three times:
 R.action ω = ∫ F_R(ω) dμ = p₁∫ F_{R₁}(ω) dμ + p₂∫ F_{R₂}(ω) dμ = p₁R₁.action ω + p₂R₂.action ω. ∎
proof_key_steps: A unit orientation v satisfies |v(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ (operator norm).
θ'ξ'(ω) is integrable on the carrier of every IMRep, dominated by sup‖ω‖·θ'1_{spt ω}.
R'.action ω = ∫ (1_{M'}θ'ξ')(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ(x).
Integrate the a.e. identity evaluated at ω(x) and use linearity of the integral.

subproblems.title: Unit orientations pair with covectors of norm ≤ 1, with a norming covector (Simon Ch. 6, 2.6(a)–(b)); reused Submission.regcomp_unit_orientation_pairing
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, ξ ∈ Λₙ(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P n) and Q a linear subspace of ℝ^P with IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q (ξ(α) = ±α(τ) for an orthonormal τ : Fin n → ℝ^P spanning Q). Then (i) |ξ(α)| ≤ |α| for every n-covector α, where |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2} is the Euclidean coefficient norm; and (ii) there is an n-covector β with |β| ≤ 1 and ξ(β) = 1.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ξ : MultiVector P n) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q → (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, |ξ α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) ∧ ∃ β : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm β ≤ 1 ∧ ξ β = 1
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1(a) of the supplied proof of the selected theorem (|ζ(α)| ≤ |α| and the Cauchy–Binet normalisation Σ_I ζ(dx^I)² = 1), in the Euclidean coefficient (inner product) norm. Equivalently, properties (a) and (b) of Simon Ch. 6, Remark 2.6 (chapter-06.txt lines 243–256) for that norm: ⟨ω, ξ⟩ ≤ |ω||ξ| for simple ξ, with equality for some ω ≠ 0. This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.regcomp_unit_orientation_pairing, reused at its byte-identical frozen type.
Notation:
 - e is the standard basis of ℝ^P, and |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2}.
 - For an orthonormal basis f = (f_b)_{b ∈ Fin P} of ℝ^P and an n-covector α, S_f(α) := Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} α(f_{j(0)}, …, f_{j(n−1)})².
1. S_e(α) = n!·|α|².
 - If j is not injective, α(e_j) = 0, since α is alternating.
 - Each injective j factors uniquely as j = I∘π, with I strictly increasing (the increasing enumeration of range j) and π a permutation of Fin n. Then α(e_j) = sign(π)α(e_I), so α(e_j)² = α(e_I)².
 - Each strictly increasing I arises from exactly n! injective j.
 Hence S_e(α) = n!·Σ_I α(e_I)² = n!·|α|². For n = 0 both sides equal α()².
2. Basis invariance: S_f(α) = S_e(α) for every orthonormal basis f.
 - Write f_a = Σ_b O_{ba}e_b with O orthogonal, so Σ_a O_{ba}O_{b'a} = δ_{bb'}.
 - By multilinearity, α(f_{a_0}, …, f_{a_{n−1}}) = Σ_b (∏_k O_{b_k a_k}) α(e_{b_0}, …, e_{b_{n−1}}).
 - Squaring and summing over a: S_f(α) = Σ_{b,b'} ∏_k (Σ_{a_k} O_{b_k a_k}O_{b'_k a_k}) α(e_b)α(e_{b'}) = Σ_{b,b'} ∏_k δ_{b_k b'_k} α(e_b)α(e_{b'}) = S_e(α).
3. Unfolding the hypothesis. There are an orthonormal τ : Fin n → ℝ^P spanning Q and ε ∈ {1, −1} with ξ(α) = ε·α(τ) for every n-covector α. In particular n ≤ P. Extend τ to an orthonormal basis f of ℝ^P with f_{ι(k)} = τ_k for an injective ι : Fin n → Fin P (Gram–Schmidt; Mathlib Orthonormal.exists_orthonormalBasis_extension).
4. Part (i). For each permutation π of Fin n, the map j = ι∘π satisfies α(f_j) = α(τ∘π) = sign(π)α(τ). These n! maps are distinct, so n!·α(τ)² ≤ S_f(α) = S_e(α) = n!·|α|² by steps 1–2. Hence |ξ(α)| = |α(τ)| ≤ |α| for every α.
5. Part (ii). Define β₀(v_0, …, v_{n−1}) := det[⟨τ_i, v_k⟩]_{i,k ∈ Fin n}.
 (a) β₀ is an n-covector: it is multilinear (column k is linear in v_k), alternating (two equal arguments give two equal columns) and continuous (ℝ^P is finite-dimensional).
 (b) β₀(τ) = det[⟨τ_i, τ_k⟩] = det I = 1.
 (c) For j : Fin n → Fin P, ⟨τ_i, f_b⟩ = 1 if b = ι(i) and 0 otherwise. So column k of [⟨τ_i, f_{j(k)}⟩] is the unit column with index ι⁻¹(j(k)) if j(k) ∈ range ι, and zero otherwise.
 (d) Hence β₀(f_j) = ±1 if j = ι∘π for a permutation π, and β₀(f_j) = 0 otherwise (a zero column or two equal columns). So S_f(β₀) = n!, and |β₀|² = S_f(β₀)/n! = 1 by steps 1–2.
 (e) Put β := ε·β₀. Then |β| = |β₀| = 1 ≤ 1 (|−α| = |α|), and ξ(β) = ε·β(τ) = ε·ε·β₀(τ) = 1.
 For n = 0, β₀ is the constant 1 and the same computation holds. ∎
proof_key_steps: The full square sum S_f(α) = Σ_j α(f_j)² equals n!|α|² for the standard basis and is the same for every orthonormal basis.
Extend τ to an orthonormal basis f; the n! terms j = ι∘π give n!α(τ)² ≤ S_f(α) = n!|α|², so |ξ(α)| ≤ |α|.
β₀ := det[⟨τ_i, ·⟩] has β₀(τ) = 1 and S_f(β₀) = n!, so |β₀| = 1; β := εβ₀ satisfies |β| ≤ 1 and ξ(β) = 1.

subproblems.title: Mass bound for an integer combination: (†) a.e. implies μ_R ≤ |p₁|μ_{R₁} + |p₂|μ_{R₂}
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, let R₁ = (M₁, θ₁, ξ₁), R₂ = (M₂, θ₂, ξ₂), R = (M, θ, ξ) be integer multiplicity triples (IMRep) in U and p₁, p₂ ∈ ℤ. Suppose that for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ ℝ^P (Hⁿ = μHE[n]) the n-vectors satisfy 1_M(x)θ(x)ξ(x) = p₁1_{M₁}(x)θ₁(x)ξ₁(x) + p₂1_{M₂}(x)θ₂(x)ξ₂(x). Then μ_R ≤ |p₁|μ_{R₁} + |p₂|μ_{R₂} as measures on ℝ^P, where μ_{R′} = θ′Hⁿ⌞M′ (IMRep.measure) and |pᵢ| = pᵢ.natAbs acts as a scalar in [0, ∞].
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R₁ R₂ R : IMRep U n) (p₁ p₂ : ℤ), (∀ᵐ x ∂μHE[n], R.carrier.indicator (fun y => (R.mult y : ℝ) • R.orient y) x = (p₁ : ℝ) • R₁.carrier.indicator (fun y => (R₁.mult y : ℝ) • R₁.orient y) x + (p₂ : ℝ) • R₂.carrier.indicator (fun y => (R₂.mult y : ℝ) • R₂.orient y) x) → R.measure ≤ (p₁.natAbs : ℝ≥0∞) • R₁.measure + (p₂.natAbs : ℝ≥0∞) • R₂.measure
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the final sentence of step 5 (0 ≤ θ ≤ |p₁|θ₁1_{M₁} + |p₂|θ₂1_{M₂}) and step 8 of the supplied proof of the selected theorem. Step 8 is reproduced in step 5 below.
Departure: the supplied proof reads the multiplicity bound off its explicit formula θ = |m|, by the triangle inequality. Here R is an arbitrary IMRep satisfying the identity (†). This is what the reused construction (sibling combination_construction) exports: (†), not its formula. So the same bound is recovered Hⁿ-a.e. from (†), using the normalisation of step 1(a) in the Euclidean coefficient norm (sibling orientation_pairing). Step 8 only integrates the bound, so an a.e. bound suffices.
Notation:
 - μ := μHE[n]; for c ∈ ℤ, |c| = c.natAbs.
 - For an IMRep R' = (M', θ', ξ') in U put g_{R'} := 1_{M'}θ' : ℝ^P → ℕ and F_{R'} := 1_{M'}θ'ξ' : ℝ^P → Λₙ(ℝ^P).
 - The hypothesis reads F_R = p₁F_{R₁} + p₂F_{R₂} μ-a.e.; μ_{R'} := R'.measure = (μ⌞M').withDensity θ'.
 - |β| := covectorEuclideanNorm β.
1. Good points. M, M₁, M₂ are Borel, so the field orients of each of R, R₁, R₂ gives: for μ-a.e. x, if x ∈ M' then ξ'(x) is a unit orientation of some subspace Q (IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ' x) Q). Let G be the set of x at which these three implications and the hypothesis identity all hold. Then μ(ℝ^P ∖ G) = 0.
2. One term. Let R' be an IMRep and x a point such that x ∈ M' implies that ξ'(x) is a unit orientation of some Q. Let β be an n-covector with |β| ≤ 1. Then |F_{R'}(x)(β)| ≤ g_{R'}(x):
 - if x ∉ M', both sides are 0;
 - if x ∈ M', then F_{R'}(x)(β) = θ'(x)·ξ'(x)(β), and orientation_pairing (i) gives |ξ'(x)(β)| ≤ |β| ≤ 1, so |F_{R'}(x)(β)| ≤ θ'(x) = g_{R'}(x).
3. Pointwise multiplicity bound. Claim: for x ∈ G, g_R(x) ≤ |p₁|g_{R₁}(x) + |p₂|g_{R₂}(x) in ℕ.
 - If x ∉ M, then g_R(x) = 0.
 - If x ∈ M, then ξ(x) is a unit orientation of some Q, since x ∈ G. orientation_pairing (ii) gives an n-covector β with |β| ≤ 1 and ξ(x)(β) = 1. Evaluating the identity at β and using step 2 for R₁ and R₂ (x ∈ G):
  θ(x) = θ(x)·ξ(x)(β) = F_R(x)(β) = p₁F_{R₁}(x)(β) + p₂F_{R₂}(x)(β) ≤ |p₁|·|F_{R₁}(x)(β)| + |p₂|·|F_{R₂}(x)(β)| ≤ |p₁|g_{R₁}(x) + |p₂|g_{R₂}(x).
 This is a real inequality between natural numbers, so it holds in ℕ. Hence
 (‡) g_R ≤ |p₁|g_{R₁} + |p₂|g_{R₂} μ-a.e.
4. Measures as integrals. For an IMRep R' and a Borel set s: μ_{R'}(s) = ∫⁻_s θ' d(μ⌞M') = ∫⁻_{s∩M'} θ' dμ = ∫⁻_s g_{R'} dμ (Mathlib withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict, lintegral_indicator). Also g_{R'} is Borel, since θ' is measurable and M' is Borel.
5. Comparison (step 8). Let s be Borel. By (‡), which holds μ⌞s-a.e. since μ⌞s ≪ μ, monotonicity of the lower integral gives the first inequality below. Additivity for measurable integrands and constants pulled out of ∫⁻ give the next equality, and step 4 the last:
 μ_R(s) = ∫⁻_s g_R dμ ≤ ∫⁻_s (|p₁|g_{R₁} + |p₂|g_{R₂}) dμ = |p₁|∫⁻_s g_{R₁} dμ + |p₂|∫⁻_s g_{R₂} dμ = |p₁|μ_{R₁}(s) + |p₂|μ_{R₂}(s).
 The right-hand side is (|p₁|•μ_{R₁} + |p₂|•μ_{R₂})(s), where the scalars |pᵢ| ∈ [0, ∞) act on measures. Two measures that compare on all Borel sets compare as measures (Mathlib Measure.le_iff). Hence R.measure ≤ (p₁.natAbs : ℝ≥0∞) • R₁.measure + (p₂.natAbs : ℝ≥0∞) • R₂.measure. ∎
proof_key_steps: A.e. on ℝ^P the hypothesis identity holds and the orientations of R, R₁, R₂ are unit orientations on their carriers.
For |β| ≤ 1 and a.e. x, |(1_{M'}θ'ξ')(x)(β)| ≤ 1_{M'}θ'(x), by orientation_pairing (i).
At a.e. x ∈ M pick β with |β| ≤ 1 and ξ(x)(β) = 1 (orientation_pairing (ii)); evaluating (†) at β gives θ(x) ≤ |p₁|1_{M₁}θ₁(x) + |p₂|1_{M₂}θ₂(x).
μ_{R'}(s) = ∫⁻_s 1_{M'}θ' dHⁿ for Borel s; integrate the a.e. bound to get μ_R(s) ≤ |p₁|μ_{R₁}(s) + |p₂|μ_{R₂}(s), hence μ_R ≤ |p₁|μ_{R₁} + |p₂|μ_{R₂}.
